commit_message:
avcodec/bsf/extract_extradata: remove extradata blocks from supported LCEVC NALUs

Given we rewrite these NALUs to remove the encoded data blocks to export as extradata,
we need to do the inverse to remove SC, GC and AI blocks to export as filtered data in
packes.

Signed-off-by: James Almer <jamrial@gmail.com>
pr_title: avcodec/bsf/extract_extradata: remove extradata blocks from supported LCEVC NALUs

findings.title: Incorrect cumulative size accounting in extract_extradata_lcevc leads to out-of-bounds write
findings.message:
In extract_extradata_lcevc(), write_lcevc_nalu() returns bytestream2_tell_p(pbc), which is the ABSOLUTE write position within the target PutByteContext after writing the current NAL, not the number of bytes written by this particular call. The code treats this return value as an incremental size and repeatedly accumulates it into *size (and filtered_size) across the NAL loop: `*size += ret;` and `filtered_size += ret;`. Because `ret` is already a running total (relative to previous writes into the same pb_extradata/pb_filtered_data buffer), summing it again on every iteration causes *size (and filtered_size) to grow much faster than the number of bytes actually written, ending up far larger than the true content length and even larger than the allocated buffer size (extradata_size / filtered_size local variables used for allocation).

This bogus, inflated size is propagated back to the caller extract_extradata_filter(), which does:
  memset(extradata + extradata_size, 0, AV_INPUT_BUFFER_PADDING_SIZE);
using the corrupted extradata_size (i.e., the caller's copy of *size) as an offset into the `extradata` buffer that was allocated with the correct (smaller) size. Since the offset used for the memset padding write is far beyond the actual allocation, this results in an out-of-bounds heap write. The same wrong value is also used later as the packet's filtered size (pkt->size = filtered_size), which can lead to further out-of-bounds reads/writes when that packet data is subsequently consumed as if it had the (incorrect) larger size.
findings.suggestion: Do not accumulate the absolute PutByteContext write position (bytestream2_tell_p) returned by write_lcevc_nalu() into a running sum. Instead, after the loop finishes writing, compute the final size directly from the PutByteContext's tell_p once (which already reflects the total bytes written), and validate it against the allocated capacity with an assertion, e.g. `*size = bytestream2_tell_p(&pb_extradata); av_assert0(*size <= extradata_size);` and similarly for the filtered buffer using `bytestream2_tell_p(&pb_filtered_data)` instead of manually summing per-NAL deltas from a value that is already cumulative.

ground_truth.root_cause: write_lcevc_nalu()'s return value (bytestream2_tell_p, an absolute position in the shared PutByteContext) was misused as an incremental per-NAL size delta and summed cumulatively across iterations, producing a grossly inflated total size that no longer matches the number of bytes actually written or the size of the allocated buffer.
